The PSI of Thilaknagar Police Station submitted charge sheet against the accused person for the offences punishable under section 406 and 420 of IPC.

. The brief facts of the prosecution case is as follows:-
The case of the prosecution is that on 24.12.2015 the accused called over his mobile No.9886287165 to CW-1 Kalyani KTM Bike Show Room telephone No.8033085594 and informed that he test drive the KTM 390 Motor Cycle and purchase the same.
Therefore, the CW-1 took the KTM Duke Motor Cycle (unregistered) bearing Engine No.590229120 and Chassis No.MD2JG4H2FC271228 vehicle from his working place KTM Banashankari Show Room value of Rs.2,30,000/- at about 7.00 PM.

When the CW-1 came to the Jayanagar East End Main Road, Near Pump House Bus Stop,
Okeyard Apartment the accused introduced himself as a Gurujal Singh and informed him that he will pay Rs.2 lakhs to CW-1 and asked him to the said vehicle for test drive.

When the CW-1 was sitting his back seat of the said motor cycle at the time of test drive the accused drove the test from Okeyard Apartment to Carmel Convent School and came back to Okeyard Apartment and informed him that there was coming some sound in the said vehicle and he want to test drive the said vehicle once again alone.

When the CW-1 get down from the said motor cycle the C.C.No.21411/2017 accused took the said vehicle for test drive and he did not came back and thereby the accused person has committed the criminal breach of trust and cheated the complainant and thereby he has committed the above offences.
After completion of the investigation the PSI of Thilaknagar Police Station has filed the charge sheet against the accused person for the offences punishable under section 406 and 420 of IPC.

13. In the instant case the PW-1 and PW-2 have turned hostile to the prosecution case and not supported to the prosecution case.
During the course of cross examination by the learned Sr. APP nothing has been elicited from their mouth.
14. In this case, the prosecution has failed to elicit anything favorable to it to prove the allegations against the accused person under sections 406 and 420 of IPC.
When these being the facts, I am of the opinion that in total the prosecution has failed to bring home the guilt of the accused person beyond all reasonable doubt.
In view of the same, this court hold Point Nos.1 and 2 in the Negative.
15. Point No.3:
For the reasons stated and finding given to point Nos.1 and 2, the following is made.
ORDER The accused person is not found guilty for the offences punishable under section 406 and 420 of IPC.
C.C.No.21411/2017 Acting under section 248(1) of Code of Criminal Procedure the accused person is hereby acquitted for the offences punishable under section 406 and 420 of IPC.
The bail bond and surety bond executed by him stands canceled.
